resources.string: Android will now show a few pop-up questions. Tap Allow on each one. Here is what each one is for, and what stops working if you say no.
Phone
Lets AirBridge know when a call is ringing or in progress, so your computer can show it and let you answer or hang up.
Calls won\'t appear on your computer, and you can\'t answer or end them from there.
Contacts
Looks the caller up in your contacts, the same way your phone does, so your computer shows their name and photo.
Your computer shows only a phone number, or “Unknown caller”.
Call logs
Android only tells an app the number of a call if it has this permission. AirBridge uses it just for the call that is ringing or being made. Your call history is never read.
Calls you make show as “Unknown caller”, and some incoming calls may too.
Notifications
Lets AirBridge show the progress of file transfers, and ask you to approve a new pairing.
Transfers run without any sign of progress, and you can miss a request to pair a new device.
Nearby devices
Lets AirBridge find your computer and other phones close to you over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi, and tell whether you are near your phone when a call comes in.
Pairing with a nearby phone over Bluetooth won\'t work, and your computer can\'t tell whether you are close to your phone when a call comes in.
Turn control back on automatically
Lets AirBridge switch remote control back on by itself after a payment app. Needs a computer, once.

Banking and payment apps refuse to take a payment while remote control is switched on. AirBridge switches remote control off when one of them opens and back on when you leave, but Android only allows that if you give AirBridge one special permission. Only a computer can give it, and you do it once.

AirBridge can still switch remote control off for payment apps, but it can\'t switch it back on. After paying you would turn it on again yourself in Accessibility settings. It also can\'t switch remote control off when none of your computers is connected.
This takes about 10 minutes with a computer and a USB cable. Tap “Show me how” and follow the steps. Not now? Skip it. You can find it again any time in Settings → Payment apps.

Why this is needed
Banking and payment apps (Paytm, PhonePe, Google Pay and others) refuse to take a payment while any accessibility service is on. AirBridge\'s remote control is one.

So AirBridge switches remote control off the moment one of those apps opens, and back on when you leave. Android only lets an app switch its own accessibility service on if you give it one special permission, and only a computer can give it. You do this once.
If you skip it, nothing else breaks. You just have to turn remote control on again yourself after each payment, and AirBridge can\'t switch it off when none of your computers is connected.
What you need
A computer (Windows, Mac or Linux)
A USB cable that carries data, not one that only charges
About 10 minutes
Turn on Developer options
Open your phone\'s Settings, then About phone. Find “Build number” (on some phones it\'s under “Software information” or “Version”) and tap it 7 times. Android says you are now a developer.
Turn on USB debugging
Go back to Settings and open Developer options. It is now in Settings → System, or in “Additional settings” on some phones. Switch on “USB debugging”.
Connect the phone to your computer
Plug the cable into the phone and the computer. If the phone asks “Allow USB debugging?”, tap Allow. Tick “Always allow from this computer” so it doesn\'t ask again.
Put adb on your computer

adb is a small, free tool from Google that lets a computer talk to a phone. First check if you already have it: open Terminal (Mac or Linux) or Command Prompt (Windows), type adb version and press Enter. If it shows a version number, go to the next step.

Give AirBridge the permission
Type this one line into Terminal or Command Prompt and press Enter. If nothing is printed, it worked.
In Windows PowerShell, type .\\ in front of adb (for example .\\adb shell …).
Check that it worked
Come back to AirBridge. This screen will say Done. You can switch USB debugging off again now; the permission stays.

If something goes wrong
“No devices found”: try another cable or USB port, unlock the phone, and set its USB mode to File transfer. Then type adb devices. Your phone should be listed.
“Unauthorized”: look at your phone and tap Allow on the USB debugging question.
“SecurityException” on Xiaomi, Redmi or POCO phones: in Developer options also switch on “USB debugging (Security settings)”, then type the line again.
You can come back to this any time: Settings → Payment apps → Turn control back on automatically.
